detail.body:
# Description

Persistent workers for different world sizes may share GPUs. Restarting only the failed worker can leave CUDA and NCCL state from another pool resident, so the retry starts under the same resource pressure.

Shut down every active pool before retrying. Pool objects remain registered and restart lazily when requested, preserving reuse on the normal path.

Fixes # (issue)

detail.title: [PyTorch][CP][CI] Reset all CP process pools before retrying a failed test

files.patch:
@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@
 import pathlib
 import logging
 import copy
+from collections.abc import Callable
 from collections import deque
 import pytest
 import torch
@@ -104,8 +105,9 @@ class PoolWorker:
     _STDERR_BUFFER_LINES = 200  # ring cap (~40 KB ceiling)
     _STDERR_TAIL_CHARS = 4000  # how much to attach to the AssertionError
 
-    def __init__(self, world_size: int):
+    def __init__(self, world_size: int, reset_all_pools: Callable[[], None]):
         self.world_size = world_size
+        self._reset_all_pools = reset_all_pools
         self.proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
         self._stderr_buf: deque[str] = deque(maxlen=self._STDERR_BUFFER_LINES)
 
@@ -221,10 +223,13 @@ def submit(self, kwargs: dict, timeout: float = POOL_SUBMIT_TIMEOUT_SEC) -> None
                         sys.stderr.flush()
                     raise
                 first_err = e
+                # Pools with different world sizes can occupy the same GPUs. Reset
+                # all pools so the retry starts without leftover CUDA/NCCL state.
+                self._reset_all_pools()
                 sys.stderr.write(
                     f"[POOL-RETRY] status=retrying test={test_id!r} "
                     f"world_size={self.world_size} attempt={attempt + 1} "
-                    f"error={msg_head!r}; respawning pool and retrying\n"
+                    f"error={msg_head!r}; reset all pools and retrying\n"
                 )
                 sys.stderr.flush()
         raise first_err  # unreachable; loop either returns or raises
@@ -297,11 +302,15 @@ def cp_pool():
     """Returns a callable: cp_pool(world_size) -> PoolWorker."""
     pools: dict[int, PoolWorker] = {}
 
+    def _reset_all_pools() -> None:
+        for pool in pools.values():
+            pool.shutdown()
+
     def _get(world_size: int) -> PoolWorker:
         if world_size > torch.cuda.device_count():
             pytest.skip(f"Test requires {world_size} GPUs, but found {torch.cuda.device_count()}")
         if world_size not in pools:
-            pools[world_size] = PoolWorker(world_size)
+            pools[world_size] = PoolWorker(world_size, _reset_all_pools)
         return pools[world_size]
 
     yield _get

inline_comments.body: **Cross-pool reset is untested** The new reset runs only after a retryable failure, so ordinary passing tests do not check it. A deterministic test with two registered pools could verify that both shut down when one retries and restart when requested. Without that test, a regression in the behavior this PR fixes may go unnoticed. **Knowledge Base Used:** [Verification and CI matrix](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/verification-and-ci.md) Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!
